newsitem.title: UK: Growth seen in European asset-backed market - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: Growth seen in European asset-backed market - Fitch.

text.p: The European asset-backed market will continue to grow in the coming years, investors and bankers were told at a conference Tuesday.

"The introduction last year of new applications and asset classes, new originators and investors should lead to continued market growth of European securitisation over the next few years," Kimberly Swalek, senior director at Fitch Investors Service said.
Britain was expected to dominate the European market, which saw nearly $35 billion of new deals in 1996, mainly because of its private finance initiative (PFI).
Under PFI, the government aims to shift the capital cost and risk of public investments into private hands.

"Anticipated PFI sales this year include a 2.0 billion stg student loan portfolio and the sale of Department of Social Security office properties," Swalek said, adding Belgium, Italy and France also had a busy pipeline of deals.
At least seven banks from around the world were looking into securitising their corporate loans to remove them from their balance sheets, she said.

Last year, National Westminster Bank launched an innovative $5.0 billion securitisation of high-quality corporate loans, which allowed the bank to re-allocate the capital to more profitable businesses.
The deal, called R.O.S.E. funding, was the first time high-quality corporate loans were used as collateral, although the U.S. market has seen similar transactions with sub-investment grade loans.
A NatWest official, also speaking at the conference, said future R.O.S.E. type securitisation programmes were expected in the market, with developments likely from the Far East.
He said banks were also looking into securitising other types of loans, like structured finance and project finance loans.
The European securitised market, active since the last 1980s, remains small relative to the more developed U.S. market.
In 1996, over $150 billion was raised in the U.S. public asset-backed market, and a further $18 billion through private issuance, Fitch figures showed.
